notes.built: 2026-10-10 by Claude for the Wikidata linking survey. Wikidata read-only (wbsearchentities, wbgetentities, list=search), at most 1 request per second with User-Agent 'lexflow-research/0.1 (https://github.com/alibama/lexflow)'; about 310 requests. Three reads of lexipedia.wikibase.cloud (Item:Q168 and its properties). Nothing was written anywhere except this file.
notes.terms: 155 normalised terms: actor names and decision inputs of curated/<state>/<question>.json and the 'steps' models of curated_ask/*/*.json, office slots and profile groups of curated_ask, and headings of curated and gold sections that name a role, document or procedure (looked up with lexflow.ask.index.lookup). 'source' names the file and field or the heading; 'domain' is the question area; 'kind' is role / document / entity type / body type / named entity / concept.
notes.search: First pass ('pass': 'first'): wbsearchentities(term, language en, limit 5); when it returned nothing, a full-text list=search(term, limit 5) ('via': 'fulltext'). Second pass ('pass': 'alternate'), only for terms whose first pass had no exact candidate: 1-3 other phrasings (synonyms, another state's name for it, spelling variants) in 'query'. Entities fetched with languages en|mul, because Wikidata now keeps many labels only under 'mul' ('label_lang'). 'p31', 'p279' and 'jurisdiction' (P1001 + P17) carry QIDs with English labels; 'sitelinks' is the sitelink count; 'rank' is the position in its own result list.
notes.label_match: Computed: 'exact' = normalised label equals the term (case, punctuation, plural s, 's and labour/labor folded); 'alias' = equals an en or mul alias; 'partial' = shares a content word with the label or an alias; 'none' otherwise.
notes.judgement: Hand labels; every pair was reviewed. exact = the same legal concept as used in the lexflow source. broader / narrower = a super- or sub-concept (per-US-state legal-form items and subclasses are narrower). related = a neighbouring concept fit for 'see also' but not the meaning (records manager for a FOIA officer, pseudonym for assumed business name). wrong = a different thing: creative works, articles, people, places, PropBank roles, genes, NARA series, a single instance (one certificate, one agency) when the term is generic, a foreign jurisdiction's namesake, or a specific statute when the term is generic.
notes.best: The candidate a linker should attach: the exact one if any (the best-described of duplicates), else the closest broader/narrower one ('best_judgement' says which); related-only terms get null. 'missed' records 4 known equivalents that no query returned because the item lacks that alias: statutory agent -> registered agent Q7309406, community supervision -> probation Q13961, work furlough -> work release Q8034639, expunction -> expungement Q2352928.

coverage.only_broader_narrower_related: 26/155 (16.8%): 9 with a usable broader/narrower link, 17 with only related candidates
coverage.pairs: 714 (term, candidate) pairs: wrong 496, related 61, exact 111, narrower 28, broader 18

notes.gaps: No Wikidata item found for: incorporator, organizer (corporate), requester, the signing 'authorized representative', custodian of public records, FOIA/records officer, exemption from disclosure, fee waiver, certificate of rehabilitation, criminal history evaluation letter, order of nondisclosure, substantial evidence rule, provisional (occupational) license, license revocation, driver's license suspension, inmate trust account, inmate welfare fund, gate money, a generic clean slate law, Article 78 proceeding, Central Criminal Records Exchange, PIECP, the Texas APA. Roles that statute headings name (Fla. Stat. 607.0201 'Incorporators.') and state-specific instruments are the weakest groups. These are the candidates for lexflow's own concept items.
false_positive_patterns: Same-title works and records: scholarly articles, films, episodes, albums, games, songs, paintings, NARA series and items, CRS reports. Always wrong, and their label often matches the term exactly.

Foreign namesakes with an exact label: limited liability company (Latvia, New Zealand, PRC), general partnership (Switzerland, France, Estonia, Canada), public body (Hungary, Spain, Netherlands, Hong Kong), attorney general (New Zealand, Uganda, Norway), statute of limitations (Italian prescrizione), child support (Finland, New Zealand).

A specific statute for a generic term: Administrative Procedure Act (US 1946, Germany, South Korea, Finland, Japan), the Adam Walsh Act for 'sex offender registration', New York's Clean Slate Act, the Speedy Trial Act, Scottish statutory instruments for 'statutory agent'.

Word-sense collisions on short role and status words: organizer (event producer, storage box, Spemann organizer), founder (metal founder, donor, Star Trek species), commissary (military official), probation (new-employee period), parole (linguistics), conviction (belief), venue (place), rehabilitation (medicine, ecology), pardon (Breton ceremony), infraction (ice-hockey foul), sheriff (Norwegian lensmann, a football club).
Linguistic and biological items: PropBank 'prototypical agent/patient' items for incorporator, scofflaw and defendant; 'serine incorporator' proteins and genes.

Alias hits on a neighbouring concept: records officer -> records manager; public information officer -> spokesperson; provisional license -> learner's permit; fictitious or assumed name -> pseudonym; principal place of business -> headquarters; custodian of records -> the federal 18 U.S.C. 2257 records custodian.
Named entities that share a name: five state Offices of Administrative Hearings, other counties' clerks, Connecticut PURA for 'public utilities commission'. Only the source's jurisdiction can pick.

Generic versus US-specific: the generic item ranks first (corporation Q167037, private limited company, secretary-of-state positions, prison for 'jail', the judicial-review doctrine) while the US concept is the exact one (Q57655560, Q149789, Q533501, county jail Q12858028, review of administrative act Q12876258).
separating_features: label_match is needed but not enough: P(exact) is 0.33 for an exact label match (86 of 257 pairs), 0.23 for an alias match, 0.03 for partial and 0.02 for none.

Junk patterns in the description or P31 (article, film, episode, album, game, name, NARA, 'Act', statute, statutory instrument, PropBank, protein, gene, disambiguation, place, building) mark 355 pairs: 349 wrong, 4 related, 2 exact.
Sitelinks: exact items have a median of 9 (7% have none); wrong items a median of 0 (59% have none); broader items a median of 25. The per-state GLEIF legal-form items (narrower) have none.
Jurisdiction: P17/P1001 outside the US marks 89 wrong against 4 exact; 'legal form in <US state>' marks narrower (15 of 22).

P31 'legal term or legal concept': 14 exact, 5 related, 3 broader, 2 wrong. P279 document, punishment, crime and name are positive. P31 position/profession/occupation is mixed (14 exact, 16 wrong) and needs the description's sense.
No P31 is normal for good concept items (50 of 111 exact have only P279), so a missing P31 is not a negative signal.
Rank: rank 1 of the term search is exact for 74 of 147 terms; ranks 3-5 hold 15 exact among 297 candidates.

Baseline rule (label or alias match, no junk pattern, no foreign or state-specific tag): pair precision 0.59, recall 0.86. Taking its first accepted first-pass candidate gives 80 correct links and 40 correct nulls out of 155 terms, with 15 false links, 13 wrong links and 7 missed exacts. The rest are sense and generic-versus-US calls. Those need the source context (heading and quote) compared with the description, for example an embedding-similarity feature.
notes.lexipedia: lexipedia.wikibase.cloud Item:Q168 is 'Fla. Stat. 607.0201' (description '607.0201 Incorporators.'; P5 instance of Q10 'statute or legal provision', P15 Florida, P22 citation, P23 official text, P25 legal identifier lexflow:statute:fl:607.0201). It does not link to the concept it defines. The Wikibase already has P8 'exact match' (skos:exactMatch, URL) for Wikidata IRIs. It has no broad, narrow or close match property and no 'defines term' property. By this survey about 70% of these terms could carry P8 to Wikidata; the 23 terms with no match, incorporator among them, would need their own concept items. Read only; nothing was written.
notes.privacy: Person items appear in this survey only as wrong search hits. One of them, a human item with no sitelinks for an apparently private individual, has its name and QID withheld ('[name withheld]', 'Q-withheld'). The alias lists of two performer items, which may hold birth names, are withheld (empty). The replacements leave every feature of the 714 pairs unchanged, so the model fitted on them is unchanged. Public figures, historical persons and a one-word label that is the searched term itself are kept as Wikidata gave them.
